description: Sample app trees and the row standards:adoption should report for one surface each. The kit test checks the surfaces and states exist; standards validates the outcomes against these trees.

cases.why: A notification through FluentMailMessage and a mail view on x-mail::message, which the kit brands.
A published resources/views/vendor/mail layout replaces the kit's branded one.
Hidden inputs (CSRF, method spoofing) and a lone search box are not hand-rolled form controls; nothing adopts the kit inputs either.
One raw form control on a page is hand-rolled; zero exemptions, so no count threshold.
Raw inputs inside the kit tree are kit-owned; the page uses the kit Input.
A raw file input sets has-file-uploads and is the hand-rolled signal: uploads go through the kit FileInput or BulkDrop.
Passkeys are optional per app: an app with sign-in screens that has not opted in to passkeys never fails the gate for them.
The user model implements Fortify's PasskeyUser and a page uses the kit's PasskeyOffer.
A card under Pages/Auth is a public sign-in frame, not a signed-in content panel.
An app *Card component outside the public pages is a hand-rolled content panel.
A *Panel file name alone (side panels, settings panels) is not evidence of content panels.
An order history list is domain data, not an activity feed; only Timeline, ActivityFeed and ActivityLog names count.
A *Chip is not a badge; user and avatar chips count toward data.avatar instead.
A sortable list alone is not a sequence editor; the workbench applies only with an editor, builder or preview screen too.
A drag-and-drop editor page with its own builder is a hand-rolled workbench.
A calendar grid is a <table> with no header row, so it is not a hand-rolled data table.
A table with a header row in a page is a hand-rolled data table.
A page that renders a list beside a detail view needs a split view.
Actions in the app layout's #header slot are page actions, as much as a page-root <header> is.
A legacy app's own PageHeader reads hand-rolled without the kit shell, which the ui.kit-shell rule needed.
A starter-kit AppLayout is a hand-rolled signed-in shell, even with no header, nav or aside at its root.

The app adopted the kit shell and renders its own header with a sign-out. ui.kit-shell would read that hand-rolled, but it needs Pest, which kit's CI doesn't install, so it is reported as skipped and no other signal fires. Apps run it from their own vendor, where Pest is installed, and --ci and --compliance fail closed on the skip.
A *Card under a content or render folder (feed/body/BodyCard.vue, ScoreCard.vue) draws content, not a page's content panel.
The shadcn primitives under resources/js/components/ui are what the kit builds on, not app menus.
The file-name signal skips resources/js/components/ui, but standards' replaces scan still reads ui/button/Button.vue as a generic Button: replaces.components takes no path filter yet.
A page uses the kit InputNumber with kind="money".
numeral formats currency by hand.
An app InputPercent component is a hand-rolled percent input.
An InputNumber of kind integer takes neither money nor a percentage; plain numbers are common and not evidence.
A bound :kind can't be read statically, so it counts as unknown and doesn't fire.
A page uses the kit AddressFieldset.
An app OptionsProvinceState component is a hand-rolled region select.
EmailAddress and IpAddress components aren't postal addresses, so the fact stays false.
Nothing in the app takes or shows a postal address.
A page uses the kit InputTags.
@sipec/vue3-tags-input is a hand-rolled tags input.
A ChipList shows chips; it isn't a tag input (data.badge and data.avatar read chips).
Nothing in the app takes tags.
A TimeAgo component on timeago.js formats dates in the app's own code.
The page shows its dates with the kit DateTime (relative and date).
A DatePicker component on @vuepic/vue-datepicker asks for dates in the app's own code.
The booking form asks for its dates with the kit InputDate and InputDateRange.
A TimePicker component asks for the opening time in the app's own code.
The booking form asks for its times with the kit InputTime.
A Blade app layout (layouts/app.blade.php) with its own nav and logout form is a hand-rolled workspace shell.
A signed-in Blade page wraps itself in <x-app-layout>, the app's own page frame.
Raw <button> elements in Blade views are hand-rolled buttons.
A Blade form with a raw text input and textarea; Blade templates count as well as Vue.
A raw <form> in a Blade view is a hand-rolled form frame.
A Blade index page renders a raw <table> with a <thead> header row.
A Blade action-message component flashes the status after a save.
A delete route with no confirmation of any kind: the Filament fact stays false without Filament code.
Livewire full-page routes in an auth group sign the app in; components/layouts/app.blade.php is its own shell.
A Livewire component view binds a raw <input> with wire:model.
A Livewire appearance settings view switches the theme itself.
A full-page component takes its layout implicitly; no Blade page names <x-layouts.app>, so nothing is evidence either way.
A Filament resource form built from TextInput, Select and Textarea under app/Filament.
A Filament resource form takes a file through FileUpload.
A Filament resource table with TextColumn columns.
Filament DeleteAction (table row and page header) confirms deletes with Filament's own modal.
A Filament page sends its own Notification after a save; the panel provider's ->login() reads app/Filament as signed-in.
A FormCard given a useSubmitForm() as :form is the kit's form frame: the card renders the <form> itself.
A raw <form> calling useSubmitForm's submit() is a hand-rolled frame: useSubmitForm alone is not the frame, FormCard or FormActions is.
